perforce.config.enabled.description: Enable the Perforce source control integration.
perforce.config.port.description: Fallback P4PORT (server:port) used when no environment variable or P4CONFIG provides one. Prefer p4 set / P4CONFIG.
perforce.config.user.description: Fallback P4USER used when no environment variable or P4CONFIG provides one.
perforce.config.client.description: Fallback P4CLIENT (workspace) used when no environment variable or P4CONFIG provides one.
perforce.config.maxConcurrent.descriptio: Maximum number of concurrent p4 processes. Each p4 command is a process spawn plus a server round-trip, so a low cap protects the server and this machine.
perforce.config.commandTimeout.descripti: Maximum lifetime of a single p4 process in seconds before it is killed; 0 disables the timeout. Bounds 'hung forever', not 'slow': a p4 stuck on a frozen network drive or a half-open gateway connection otherwise holds its concurrency slot indefinitely.
perforce.config.refreshInterval.descript: Seconds between background refreshes of the pending changelists. 0 disables polling (recommended for large depots); use explicit Refresh instead.
perforce.config.autoEdit.description: Automatically open a file for edit (p4 edit) on its first local modification. Off by default — opening files for edit is a server operation.
perforce.config.reconcileHint.enabled.de: Mark files in the Explorer that are changed on disk but not opened yet with an RC badge. Only the rows currently on screen are checked (p4 reconcile -n on those paths), so the cost scales with what you can see rather than with the size of the depot; the scope follows your focus folders. Turn it off to stop the Explorer from triggering reconcile scans at all.
perforce.config.reconcileLimit.descripti: Maximum number of working-tree drift rows listed in the "Changes" group. Files whose disk content diverges from the depot but that are not opened in any changelist are listed there; beyond this count the list is truncated (the group title says so and the Perforce output channel logs it). Mirrors git.statusLimit: assigning the whole group is proportional to its size, so a very large list costs more than it informs.
perforce.config.reconcileScan.maxBatchDu: Ceiling for one directory batch of the background working-tree scan (p4 reconcile -n, dry-run) that tints folders in the Explorer ahead of their files being opened. A directory batch slower than this is split into its direct subdirectories, so batches converge to roughly this duration. The scan runs at background priority, is resumable across restarts, and can be cancelled from the status bar.
perforce.config.reconcile.excludeFolders: Folders to ignore when running reconcile (including background warmup scans, Explorer hint detection, and right-clicking a folder to collect changes). Supports relative or absolute paths. Collecting an ancestor directory carves out nested excluded folders. Changes apply to commands and Explorer badges immediately; only the background warmup scan reruns with the new configuration after a window reload.
perforce.config.cache.enabled.descriptio: Cache p4 and Swarm results to cut server round-trips. Immutable p4 data persists across sessions; mutable workspace and review data uses a short TTL and is invalidated after any change.
perforce.config.cache.workspaceTtl.descr: Milliseconds a cached workspace query (opened files, file mappings) stays valid before it is re-fetched. Cache is always invalidated after a mutation, so this only bounds staleness from changes made outside the editor. 0 disables workspace caching (immutable-history caching still applies).
perforce.config.cache.diskLimitMb.descri: Maximum size (MB) of the on-disk cache for immutable history data. Least-recently-used entries are evicted past this cap. 0 disables disk persistence (in-memory caching still applies).
perforce.config.openedByOthers.autoCheck: Periodically ask the server in the background which files other clients have open and grey-mark them in the Explorer, so a file someone else is editing is visible before you start on it — for binary game assets that cannot be merged this matters more than the revision number. On by default. The scan (p4 opened -a) runs at background priority and never blocks a click, but it reads the server's open table, whose size depends on the whole team's activity — on a very busy shared server, turn it off and check with teammates instead.
perforce.config.openedByOthers.intervalS: Minimum seconds between two automatic opened-by-others scans. Minimum 30s: each scan is a server round-trip over the sync scope, so a short interval would turn every save into one.
perforce.config.timeline.showPending.des: Show an entry for the file's pending changes (opened, or modified on disk without being opened) at the top of the Timeline view.

perforce.config.swarm.enabled.descriptio: Enable the Swarm (P4 Code Review) integration.
perforce.config.swarm.url.description: Swarm server URL. Credentials are never stored here — Swarm reuses the p4 login ticket.
perforce.config.swarm.apiVersion.descrip: Swarm REST API version segment (default v9 — its endpoint set is the most complete, including the action dashboard; use v11 only if your server requires it).
perforce.config.swarm.pollInterval.descr: Seconds between background polls for review updates (drives new-review notifications, the Activity Bar badge and the status bar count). 0 uses the default 60s. Minimum 10s.
perforce.config.swarm.backgroundPoll.ena: Periodically poll the Swarm dashboard in the background (drives new-review notifications, the Activity Bar badge and the status bar count). Off by default — the reviews list still refreshes whenever it is opened or via its manual Refresh button.
perforce.config.swarm.reviewWindowDays.d: Only list reviews updated within this many days in the Swarm Reviews view; ignored reviews older than this are automatically removed from the Ignored list. 0 shows all reviews with no time limit.
perforce.config.swarm.authMode.descripti: How Swarm authenticates: 'ticket' reuses the p4 login ticket (default), 'token' uses an independent Swarm API token from secret storage.
perforce.config.swarm.trace.description: Log verbose Swarm diagnostics (request bodies, query params, retries, timings, error response bodies) to the Swarm output channel. Credentials are never logged. Use when troubleshooting.
